title:
The Girl Who
Chose Hare
description: Abandoned in the forest and rescued with a wounded hand, a girl remembers who helped her when others could not.

source.adaptation: Original Hypa retelling of the documented folktale; see SOURCES.md.

lines.text: A girl went into the forest with her companions to gather firewood.
ask: Why does the girl go into the forest?

lines.text: She climbed a tree, slipped, and trapped her hand in the wood.
Her companions were jealous of her skill at finding wood. They left her behind and denied seeing her.
Alone in the forest, the girl sang whenever she heard a sound.
A hunter heard her song. Later he brought it back to the village, where her family recognized her voice.
People took tools into the forest and freed the girl from the tree.
ask: How does her family find her?

lines.text: But her trapped hand had become badly wounded.
Her mother promised that whoever healed her daughter could marry her.
Monkey, Panther, Lion, and others tried, but none could heal the wound.
At last Hare was allowed to try. He used remedies from the land around them.
Hare succeeded, and the girl recovered.
When suitors came, she refused even those with wealth and noble standing.
She chose Hare, who had helped her when others could not.
She remembered his kindness and honoured the promise her mother had made.
The lesson is to value help, loyalty, and honesty above riches or rank.
That is the story of the girl who chose Hare.
